hero.lead: A nation of 35.1 million that completed its IMF programme in July 2026 after growth of 6 percent in 2025, and with a new $500 million road plan for its farms.

capital.heading: Ghana has rebuilt its credit, review by review. Next, a safe toilet in every home.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility, final review
register.note: Final disbursement of about $371 million; a 36-month Policy Coordination Instrument requested
register.text: Ghana completed every review, and asked the IMF to keep certifying its reforms without new lending.

register.name: Secondary Education Transformation for Access, Relevance, and Results for Jobs (STARR-J)
register.note: About 2.2 million students in almost 1,000 public secondary schools
register.text: Rehabilitates, upgrades and builds secondary classrooms across the country, and strengthens core subjects, digital skills and technical and vocational training. It responds to the double-track system, whose long breaks in attendance have disrupted learning. It serves the education standard.

register.name: Ghana Market Access and Connectivity Project
register.note: More than 1,000 km of rural feeder roads in nine regions
register.text: Rehabilitates and maintains more than 1,000 km of rural feeder roads in nine regions, from Upper West to Western. It is to benefit more than 550,000 people, about 350,000 of them farmers, and create some 25,000 short-term jobs. It links food and livelihood to markets.

register.name: Climate-resilient landscapes for sustainable livelihoods in northern Ghana (FP265)
register.detail: Approved 3 July 2025 · Grant · $10.1M disbursed by 30 April 2026 · Completion 2032
register.note: Grant; total value $70.2 million with co-financing
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant, through UNEP, for smallholder farmers in northern Ghana: climate information, climate-resilient farming, restored landscapes and better access to finance. About 3.6 million people are expected to gain resilience. It protects food and livelihood against drought and flood.

register.name: Second Resilient Recovery Development Policy Financing
register.detail: Approved 27 June 2025 · Disbursed September 2025 · IDA · Second of a series
register.text: World Bank budget support for the reforms that restored fiscal sustainability, steadied the financial sector and put the energy sector on a sounder financial footing. It is the second operation in the Resilient Recovery series.

register.name: West Africa Food System Resilience Program, second phase, additional financing
register.detail: Approved 29 April 2025 · IDA credit and a Food Systems 2030 trust fund grant
register.note: Replenishes support diverted to farmers hit by floods and drought
register.text: Additional financing for Ghana’s part of the regional food system resilience programme. It replenishes resources diverted to farmers hit by floods and drought, and funds digital advisory services, climate-resilient farming, tomato production and regional food trade. It serves the food standard.

register.name: First Resilient Recovery Development Policy Financing
register.detail: Approved 23 January 2024 · Disbursed March 2024 · IDA · First of a planned series of three
register.note: Budget support after the agreement with official creditors
register.text: The first World Bank budget-support operation of Ghana’s recovery, approved after the agreement with official creditors. It supports revenue mobilisation, spending control, financial-sector stability, energy-sector finances and social protection.

register.name: Ghana Shea Landscape Emission Reductions Project (FP114)
register.detail: Approved 20 August 2020 · Grant · Total value $54.5M with Government and private co-financing
register.note: Grant to restore savanna forest and shea parklands
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant, with UNDP and the Forestry Commission, to restore 200,000 hectares of savanna forest and 300,000 hectares of shea parklands in northern Ghana. It is to reach more than 500,000 people and open new income for women in the shea trade.

register.name: Regional West Africa Resilient Rice Value Chains (REWARD) Project
register.detail: Board approval announced 3 August 2026 · Grant · Northern Savannah Ecological Zone
register.note: Grant for rice production, irrigation and processing
register.text: An African Development Bank grant for climate-resilient rice: inputs and mechanisation, irrigation and land development, modern processing and market links in the Northern Savannah Ecological Zone. It aims to reduce Ghana’s dependence on rice imports, for the food standard.

register.name: Strengthening Institutions for Enhanced Financial and Economic Governance (SIEFEG)
register.detail: Announced 8 April 2026 · African Development Fund grant · Extends a project approved in 2019
register.note: Revenue mobilisation and oversight of public spending
register.text: An African Development Fund grant to strengthen domestic revenue mobilisation and the oversight of public spending, and to prepare Ghana’s next national development plan. It builds capacity in the Ministry of Finance, the National Development Planning Commission, the Audit Service, Parliament and the Public Procurement Authority.

register.name: Cocoa risk participation facility with Absa Bank Ghana
register.detail: Announced 16 September 2026 · Unfunded risk participation · With the GAFSP Private Sector Window
register.note: Up to $50 million; traceable cocoa from more than 139,000 smallholders
register.text: IFC and the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program share the risk on Absa Bank Ghana’s lending to licensed buying companies that buy traceable cocoa from farmers in the buying season. It is expected to support more than 139,000 smallholder farmers, for livelihood.

register.name: Convertible loan to Complete Farmer
register.detail: Announced 16 September 2026 · With $480,000 of advisory support · GAFSP Business Investment Financing Track
register.note: Input finance and agronomy for farmers
register.text: An IFC convertible loan, backed by GAFSP, to scale Complete Farmer’s input financing and agronomy services. The Ghanaian agtech company serves more than 72,000 farmers across eight regions and expects to support 240,000 by 2030. It serves food and livelihood.

register.name: Guarantee for Standard Chartered Bank Ghana
register.detail: Signed 24 February 2026 · Three years · Covers reserves held at the Bank of Ghana
register.note: Frees capital for up to $307.6 million of new lending
register.text: A MIGA guarantee against the expropriation of reserves that Standard Chartered’s Ghana subsidiary holds at the Bank of Ghana. Lower risk-weights free capital for up to $307.6 million of new loans, mainly trade and corporate finance, for livelihood.

register.name: Cocoa risk-sharing facility with Access Bank Ghana
register.detail: Announced 23 January 2026 · Unfunded risk participation · With the GAFSP Private Sector Window
register.note: Up to $134 million of lending to cocoa buying companies
register.text: IFC and GAFSP cover up to $67 million of the risk on Access Bank Ghana’s working-capital loans to licensed buying companies, which can then extend up to $134 million. It funds the purchase of traceable cocoa from smallholders and more timely payments to farmers.

register.name: Cocoa risk-sharing facility with Société Générale Ghana
register.detail: Announced 20 June 2025 · Local-currency loan through an unfunded risk-sharing facility
register.note: Up to $80 million for cocoa buying companies
register.text: An IFC local-currency facility of up to $40 million equivalent that supports up to $80 million of Société Générale Ghana’s financing for licensed buying companies, and up to $320 million of cocoa trade over four years. About 75,000 smallholder farmers are expected to benefit.

register.name: Solar for Industries, LMI Holdings
register.detail: Announced 12 February 2025 · First tranche of a $100M loan facility · 150 MW of solar for the Tema and Dawa industrial zones
register.text: IFC finance for a 150 MW solar plant serving more than 100 businesses in the Tema and Dawa industrial zones, from food processing to steel and textiles. It is expected to avoid about 120,000 tonnes of carbon a year and lower power costs, for energy and livelihood.

register.name: Clean Cooking Outcome Bond
register.detail: Priced 5 December 2025 · $200M IBRD bond, matures 31 March 2032 · Variable coupon from carbon credits
register.note: About $30.5 million of private capital for clean cookstoves in Ghana
register.text: A World Bank outcome bond whose investors forgo part of their coupon to finance UpEnergy’s clean cookstove projects in Ghana, which aim to bring cleaner cooking to 1.3 million people. The emission reductions are sold to Switzerland’s KliK Foundation under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. It serves the energy standard, which is measured by clean cooking.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 59 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A lively street market in Accra, Ghana, colourful stalls

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Cocoa trees with ripening yellow pods on a smallholder farm in Ghana

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Tropical rainforest canopy of Kakum National Park, Ghana

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Below the scarcity line of 1,000 cubic metres: every drop must be stored, treated and reused.
items.alt: Lake Volta, Ghana, wide calm water with a wooden fishing canoe

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of energy from renewables, 2021
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: The Akosombo hydropower dam on the Volta River, Ghana

items.name: Complete Farmer
items.text: A Ghanaian agtech platform linking more than 72,000 farmers in eight regions with buyers, finance, inputs and agronomy, through eight fulfilment centres. IFC lent it $2.4 million in September 2026.

items.name: Safe Water Network Ghana
items.text: Runs 112 water stations in more than 150 communities, reaching about 510,000 people, nearly 15,000 of them through connections at home.

items.name: Solar for Industries, LMI Holdings
items.text: Built a 16.82 MW rooftop solar plant in the Tema Free Zone and is building 150 MW of solar for the Tema and Dawa industrial zones, with IFC finance.

items.name: Ashesi University
items.text: A university in Berekuso with 1,830 students in 2026, 53 in every hundred of them on scholarships, and 3,384 alumni.

items.name: Nyaho Medical Centre
items.text: A Ghanaian healthcare provider with its main hospital in Accra. IFC lent it $5.2 million in 2020 to open primary and urgent care in Tema, Takoradi and Kumasi.
